condition: bothersome perimenopausal night sweats and hot flushes waking patient 4 times nightly
level_rationale: Waking up 4 times every night for 3 months soaked in sweat from hot flushes and night sweats despite sleeping in a cool bedroom in a 50-year-old woman represents persistent sleep-disrupting vasomotor symptoms warranting a routine outpatient clinic visit for clinical evaluation and discussion of perimenopausal symptom management rather than home self-care alone or emergency care, whereas waking up in that cool bedroom feeling mildly warm from a single hot flush 2 weeks ago represents a benign isolated nocturnal vasomotor episode needing only routine home self-care.

design_note: Three atomic reference facts cover age 50 female speaker, sleeping in a cool bedroom, and waking 4 times nightly for 3 months soaked from hot flushes and night sweats without naming perimenopause or menopause, with a 2-word span difference (15 vs 17 words). Overriding plan.json's unrelated cardiac chest/jaw swap under Rule A first choice and Rule D, reducing f3 to waking up feeling mildly warm from a single hot flush 2 weeks ago stays nocturnal in the cool bedroom with zero new sites or triggers and shifts care cleanly from clinic evaluation (level 2) to routine self-care (level 1).
